answer: By anchoring Juniper nodes in a collateralized vault where bonded Timber must be permanently destroyed upon slashing or zero-knowledge VDF rejection, the protocol enforces strict capital scarcity. Quadratic staking protocols mathematically escalate marginal attack costs, ensuring that excessive capital expenditure per new node yields diminishing extraction value relative to the locked Timber. This negative expected utility constructs a robust Nash equilibrium guaranteeing protocol consensus stability.
